shouldFix.title: TC-PATH.unicode-norm-duplicate is still masked by the entrypoint-absent arm, so the one path class the schema calls invisible at the rendered-text level can be passed without implementing it
detail: I extracted the entrypoint and every tree path for all thirteen TC-PATH fixtures. Twelve now isolate their own arm cleanly, which is a real repair: the violating bytes have been moved into the entrypoint itself, so absolute carries entrypoint '/bin/entry', backslash carries 'bin\\entry', dot carries 'bin/./entry', dotdot carries 'bin/../entry', drive-letter carries 'C:/bin/entry', empty-segment carries 'bin//entry', non-nfc carries the NFD 'bin/caf\u0065\u0301', and nul carries 'bin/ent\u0000ry' - and in every one of those the entrypoint is present in the committed tree, so the entrypoint-presence rule cannot fire.

unicode-norm-duplicate is the exception. Its entrypoint is 'bin/entry' and its tree entries are exactly ['bin', 'bin/caf\u00e9' (NFC), 'bin/cafe\u0301' (NFD)]. 'bin/entry' is not among them, so the manifest independently trips RJ-3's 'entrypoint not present in the committed tree' clause in addition to the Unicode-normalization-duplicate clause it exists to test.

Its two sibling duplicate-path fixtures do it correctly and show the intended pattern: byte-duplicate keeps 'bin/entry' in the tree alongside its duplicate pair, and case-fold-duplicate keeps 'bin/entry' alongside 'bin/Entry'. Only unicode-norm-duplicate dropped the entrypoint entry.
The expected outcome 'RJ-3' remains literally correct, because RJ-3 carries no subcodes. The defect is discriminating power, not labelling.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: This is SATISFIED-GRADE acceptance evidence for DR-103's exact-byte cell, and the Unicode-normalization-duplicate arm is the one schemas.v11 singles out as existing only as pinned bytes because it is indistinguishable at the rendered-text level. As authored, an implementation that checks entrypoint presence and never NFC-normalizes paths for comparison passes this fixture. The corpus would then be recorded as evidence for a rule it does not actually exercise.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: One fixture of thirteen, down from the eight I found masked in corpus v1, and the correct pattern already exists twice in the same class. Nothing is mis-stated: the fixture's recorded expectation is accurate, and the class member is present rather than missing.
shouldFix.remedy: Add a 'bin/entry' file entry to the committed tree so the entrypoint resolves, leaving the NFC/NFD pair as the sole violation - exactly what byte-duplicate and case-fold-duplicate already do.

repairVerification.howIChecked: TC-ACCEPT.maximal.manifest.json now carries capabilities [{capabilityId 'host.analyze.typescript', roleSubprotocol 'opaque.analyze', subprotocolVersion 1, declarationData {}}], permissions [{permission 'host.fs.read-project', reason 'read project sources'}], and a configuration block with namespace, a JSON-Schema-subset schema and classifications mapping 'strictness' to the host-owned token 'host.analysis.non-identity'. Its root CommandSpec now carries aliases, args, options, outputModes, scope and visibility, so args is populated too. displayName and aliases remain. prerequisites stays absent from maximal, which is correct - the class lists the DR-119 prerequisite block as the separate approved-exception member, and I confirmed TC-ACCEPT.approved-exception.manifest.json carries the full eight-field shape including exceptionApprovalRef, typedAbsenceBehavior and typedFailureBehavior.

repairVerification.finding: FX-B2 (my corpus v1 blocker) - three required TC-NAME members unauthored: the alias form of the reserved claim, ALIAS_COLLISION as distinct from alias-shadows-live, and PARENT_LINKAGE_COLLISION
repairVerification.howIChecked: TC-NAME grew from 14 members to 17 and every RJ-2 subcode now has its own fixture with its own expected subcode. The three I named are present by name and by expectation: TC-NAME.reserved-alias expects RJ-2/ALIAS_SHADOWS_LIVE_OR_RESERVED, TC-NAME.alias-collision expects RJ-2/ALIAS_COLLISION and is now distinct from the separately authored TC-NAME.alias-shadows-live, and TC-NAME.parent-linkage-collision expects RJ-2/PARENT_LINKAGE_COLLISION. The class also now maps subcodes one-to-one rather than collapsing several members onto a bare 'RJ-2'.

repairVerification.finding: FX-B3 (my corpus v1 blocker) - stale-alias-after-window encoded a premature retirement violating D-012 clause 5's 90-day floor, asserted non-resolve while the date clock was still running, and carried no release-clock datum
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED - VERIFIED, and I re-did the arithmetic
repairVerification.howIChecked: The after-window index now sets deprecatedAtDate 2026-01-01 with windowEndsNoEarlierThan 2026-04-02. The 90-day floor from 2026-01-01 is 2026-04-01 in a non-leap year, so the declared window end is at or beyond the floor rather than 60 days short of it as in v1. The packet's asOf is 2026-08-14, comfortably past that, so the date clock is elapsed. The release clock is now evaluable because the packet carries hostCoreVersion 0.2.0 against deprecatedAtRelease 0.1.0 - the datum that was entirely missing before - and the packet states the reasoning in its own note. The entry status is 'retired' and its namesSnapshot.aliases is empty, consistent with retirement, and the expectation is 'RJ-2 typed non-resolve', typed rather than a silent rebind. The inside-window sibling is correct on both clocks in the other direction: deprecatedAtDate 2026-06-01 with windowEndsNoEarlierThan 2026-12-01 (past its own 2026-08-30 floor), asOf inside the window, hostCoreVersion 0.1.0 equal to deprecatedAtRelease so the release clock has not turned, status 'deprecated-alias-window' with the alias still in namesSnapshot, and expectation RESOLVE. Both edges are now exercised and both clocks are decidable.

repairVerification.finding: FX-B4 (my corpus v1 blocker) - the ACCEPT indexes silently resolved the then-open V2-A1 advisory about same-stableId multi-version coexistence
repairVerification.howIChecked: The question is no longer open: schemas.v11 carries the collisionUniverse sentence as accepted content under D-104, keying index entries per (stableId, version, scope). I checked every index fixture against that key and found no duplicate (stableId, version, scope) tuple anywhere. The multi-version pair sits at 1111.../0.0.1 and 1111.../0.0.2, both active, same scope - lawful coexistence. TC-NAME.index-scope-precedence is the case that previously could not be keyed at all: it now carries the same stableId at the same version 0.0.1 under scope 'global' and scope 'project', which the three-part key admits, and its shadowedBy is the full triple {stableId, version, scope} rather than the old pair, so the reference addresses a unique entry. The corpus now conforms to an accepted rule instead of assuming an unresolved advisory.

repairVerification.finding: FX-S1 (my corpus v1 SHOULD-FIX) - the digest-mismatch flip landed inside manifest.name and so tripped RJ-2/ROOT_COMMAND_NAME_MISMATCH as well as RJ-4/DIGEST_MISMATCH
repairVerification.howIChecked: I byte-compared TC-SIG.digest-mismatch.manifest.json against TC-ACCEPT.minimal.manifest.json: exactly one differing byte, same length 2100, at offset 251, 0x6d to 0x6e, inside the value of commands[0].description ('mounted root' becomes 'nounted root'). The flipped manifest's name is still 'fixture-min' and its parent-less command is still 'fixture-min', so the rootNameBinding invariant holds and only the digest family can fire. The packet records the recorded digest as the unflipped source's 6f8203ff... and now names the field it flipped. This is the remedy I proposed, applied precisely.

repairVerification.finding: FX-S2 (my corpus v1 SHOULD-FIX) - three RJ-2 collision fixtures were bare manifests with no packet supplying the live index their expected outcome depends on
repairVerification.howIChecked: Every collision-class TC-NAME member that needs live custody now has an admission-against-index packet carrying both indexPath and manifestPath: live-name-collision, alias-collision, alias-shadows-live, hostile-double-mount, reserved-root and reserved-alias. The intra-manifest members correctly have none, because alias-cycle, parent-cycle, unknown-parent, parent-linkage-collision, multiple-roots, root-name-mismatch and id-version-not-distinct are decidable from manifest bytes alone. The reserved-list parity case additionally gained a retained live-grammar side: TC-NAME.live-grammar-observation.json holds the observed reservedRootCommands, and the parity packet pins it by path and digest, so both operands of the comparison are now bytes in the corpus rather than one side being assumed.

It moves out of authored[] into supportingBytes[] with no 'expected' key at all, and is separately catalogued under deferredUntilDR111 with standing DEFERRED-UNTIL-DR-111 and the note that no lock fixture is required or producible until DR-111. That matches the accepted schemas.v11 position that no lock of any form is producible until DR-111 closes. The retained bytes are honest supporting material rather than scored evidence, and the note records that the retained file keeps dummy.onebyte with a differing recorded digest.

advisories.title: The reserved-list parity case authors only the equal-lists arm, so a checker that never compares still passes
advisories.detail: TC-NAME.reserved-list-live-grammar-parity.packet.json now pins both operands - the index at TC-ACCEPT.index-with-minimal.json and the live grammar at TC-NAME.live-grammar-observation.json with its digest - which is a real improvement over corpus v1, where one side was assumed. Both lists read ['help','version','doctor'], so the expectation 'ACCEPT iff reservedRootCommands equals observed reservedRootCommands' resolves to ACCEPT and is decidable from retained bytes. The residue is that only the passing arm exists: a parity check whose sole fixture has the lists already equal cannot detect a checker that never performs the comparison. A divergent-list companion would close it. Advisory rather than a finding because the class member the schema requires is the parity check itself, and it is now authored with both sides retained.
advisories.notBlocking: Both operands are pinned bytes and the stated outcome follows from them.
